feature: Clips snap to markers, and a marker drags to a new moment
summary: Markers now work like Premiere's. A clip slid or trimmed near a marker catches on it, and so does the playhead dragged along the ruler. A marker put down in the wrong place can be dragged along the ruler to a new moment, catching on cuts and the playhead, as one undo step.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next, no flag changed from its default. Open any recording; snapping (the magnet, S) is on by default.

try.do: Click the ruler at about 0:02 and press M to drop a marker there.
Click the ruler further left, then drag the clip right until its start nears the marker.
Drag the clip's right edge in toward the marker and watch it catch there.
Drag the playhead along the ruler past the marker; it catches on it.
Park the playhead at 0:06, then press the marker's flag and drag it toward the playhead.
Press ⌘Z once: the marker goes back where it was.
Click a marker's flag: the playhead jumps exactly onto it.
Press S to turn snapping off and repeat a drag: nothing catches on the marker.

evaluate: Does a clip catching on a marker feel like the same pull it gets from the playhead, no stronger and no weaker?
When the playhead is standing on a marker, a press there takes the playhead (Premiere's rule). Is that what you expect, or should the marker win?
Does the left-right arrow over a marker's flag tell you it can be dragged?
Is the green catch line enough to tell you a clip caught on a marker, or do you want the words beside it?
rough: No mock draws markers being dragged or caught on, so Premiere is the reference here.

The words 'caught on a marker at 0:02' are in the bar's spoken readout (what VoiceOver and the walks read), not drawn on screen. That is how every catch works today, the playhead's included: on screen it is the green catch line.
A marker just dropped with M sits under the playhead, and a press there drags the playhead, as in Premiere. To drag that marker you move the playhead off it first.
A marker dropped onto another becomes one marker, since markers have no names yet and two on one frame are the same mark.
The marker drag shows no capsule with its time while it moves, the same as dragging an end of the In/Out band.
